posts.title: Chip Industry Week In Review
posts.summary:
Lam Research and ASE expansions; data center shifts; CPO system architecture initiative; 2D-transistor interface solution; USENIX HW security; patent suits; image sensors; programmable AI memtransistor; Nvidia's new plan; earnings; Tier IV's L4 auto chip.
The post Chip Industry Week In Review appeared first on Semiconductor Engineering.
bullets: ASE subsidiary SPIL is investing $3.1 billion in a new Taiwan-based facility to expand CoWoS advanced packaging capacity, with production slated for 2028.
Lam Research announced a $3 billion, five-year R&D expansion plan to increase its experimental capacity by over 50%, alongside a workforce development partnership with NY Creates.
Data center infrastructure is undergoing a fundamental shift toward 1-megawatt racks, necessitating significant changes in power delivery, cooling, and the integration of optical interconnects.
Rhodium Group projects that China's legacy semiconductor capacity will approach 50% of global output by 2030, even as the nation faces ongoing restrictions on leading-edge AI chip access.
Industry experts are increasingly advocating for smaller, open-source AI models that reduce the reliance on massive data centers by enabling efficient performance on local hardware.

posts.title: 2026.33: The CapEx Train Keeps Rolling
posts.summary: The best Stratechery content from the week of August 10, 2026, including the capital constraint, AI writing, and a tale of two cities.
bullets: The AI industry is shifting from compute and power constraints to a potential capital constraint, as current AI investments have yet to demonstrate clear self-sustaining profitability.
Nvidia is employing new financial engineering mechanisms to access long-duration capital, while Google is increasingly utilizing equity markets to bridge the gap toward sustainable AI revenue.
The EU's mandate requiring AI-generated content labeling faces criticism for being impractical and potentially ineffective, as societal norms regarding AI output are expected to evolve rapidly.

New York City's finance sector remains resilient due to powerful network effects, contrasting with Hollywood's vulnerability to industry outsourcing as production hubs relocate to more favorable jurisdictions.

posts.title: Li Auto's chip ambitions extend from assisted driving to data centers, report says
posts.summary:
Li Auto is exploring an in-house cloud inference chip, and the project is still at an early stage.
For details, please visit CnEVPost (cnev.co).
bullets: Li Auto is in the early stages of developing an in-house cloud inference chip to handle workloads currently managed by GPUs.
The project aims to leverage the dataflow architecture used in the company's vehicle-side assisted driving chips to reduce R&D costs through shared design and software tools.

While technically feasible, the company faces significant challenges in achieving cost-competitive inference, which requires managing complex cloud-specific demands like dynamic batching and cluster scheduling.

posts.title: Li Auto's L6 tops 400,000 cumulative deliveries as revamped model revives demand
posts.summary:
The Li L6 delivered about 9,000 units in the first half of August, compared with just 2,716 for the whole of July, based on CnEVPost-compiled data.
For details, please visit CnEVPost (cnev.co).
bullets: Li Auto's L6 SUV has surpassed 400,000 cumulative deliveries, reaching this milestone in less than 27 months since its initial launch.
The model experienced a sharp demand rebound in August, with approximately 9,000 units delivered in the first half of the month following the July 20 launch of a revamped version.
The updated L6 features significant technical upgrades, including a larger 51 kWh battery for a 300 km all-electric range and the integration of the in-house Mach M100 assisted driving chip.

posts.title: Geely Farizon's first overseas plant starts operations in Indonesia
posts.summary:
The first locally assembled V8E all-electric logistics vehicle rolled off the line on August 13 at a plant about 80 kilometers southeast of Jakarta.
For details, please visit CnEVPost (cnev.co).
bullets: Geely Farizon has commenced operations at its first overseas knock-down (KD) plant in Indonesia, located southeast of Jakarta.
The facility has begun local assembly of the V8E all-electric logistics vehicle, which has been specifically calibrated for local road conditions and tropical climates.
This move represents a strategic shift toward localized production to bypass import tariffs, streamline supply chains, and meet tightening local content requirements in Southeast Asia.
